findings.title: Referer-only host check is spoofable and sets X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL
findings.body: Embedding authorization relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header, which non-browser clients can forge. The response is then marked X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL, so any site can frame it. A page can also be framed with no referer, which is rejected. The check is weak as an access control, and combined with ALLOWALL it is the only gate.

findings.title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever to be invoked, but the controller enqueues a job
findings.body: The controller calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...), while the spec expects TopicRetriever.new/retrieve to be called directly. Unless jobs run inline in tests, the spec fails. In addition, the controller never calls TopicRetriever itself.

findings.title: Missing topic after embed lookup leaves @topic_view nil or errors
findings.body: TopicView.new raises if the topic was deleted but the embed row remains, giving a 500/404 in the iframe. Also, in the else branch `render 'loading'` is followed by discourse_expires_in, which is fine, but the retrieval is enqueued on every request for an unknown URL, so retries can flood the queue before the throttle applies.

findings.title: Unescaped referer interpolated into inline JavaScript
findings.body: request.referer is attacker-controlled and is written inside a single-quoted JS string. ERB HTML escaping does not stop quote characters from breaking out in a JS context in every case, and the value is a full URL rather than an origin. Use `to_json` on a validated origin. This is an XSS risk and also makes postMessage targetOrigin invalid when the referer includes a path.

findings.title: contents mutated with << and URL interpolated unescaped
findings.body: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string, so it breaks on frozen strings. In poll_feed it also mutates feed item content. The url is inserted into HTML without escaping. The sha1 is computed over the content including the appended footer, which is consistent, but the mutation is fragile.

findings.title: open(url) on user-supplied URL (SSRF / command execution)
findings.body: Kernel#open with open-uri on a URL derived from a request parameter. Hosts are checked against embeddable_host, but a string starting with '|' is not a URL and is rejected only by earlier checks; relying on these is fragile. Redirects can reach internal hosts. Use a dedicated HTTP client with timeouts.

findings.title: Feed item content can be nil and crashes the whole poll
findings.body: i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when an item has no content (many RSS feeds use description). One bad item aborts the import of all remaining items. Also, `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no timeout.

findings.title: Weak origin check using indexOf
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, so an origin like 'http://a' matches any URL containing it, and an empty origin always matches. Compare for equality against the parsed origin.

findings.title: Editing an old migration with force: true drops existing table
findings.body: Changing an already-released migration to `force: true` is unrelated to this feature and would drop data if re-run. Similarly, the whitespace edit to the word counts migration is unrelated noise.
